title: Safeguards to Protect Members of Public from Recalcitrant Sex Offenders
what_it_is: Safeguards to Protect Members of Public from Recalcitrant Sex Offenders

sections.label: CT and PD sentence ranges
sections.summary: CT sentences range from five to 14 years and PD sentences range from seven to 14 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: CT sentences can range from five to 14 years and PD sentences can range from seven to 14 years.

sections.label: Minimum jail sentence framework
sections.summary: The proposal's framework is that offenders will serve a minimum jail sentence of five to 20 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The proposal is not quite fleshed out yet but the framework or the outline is that offenders will have to serve a minimum jail sentence, which could be anywhere between five and 20 years.

sections.label: Assessing cases and public feedback
sections.summary: Some cases can only be assessed at release, and public feedback was sought in July last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, really, we can only assess some of these cases at the point of release.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We sought public feedback on these proposals in July of last year.

sections.label: MAS community support and supervision
sections.summary: MAS provides community support, counselling, case management and supervision up to two years for released higher-risk inmates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The MAS provides community support, counselling, case management, with supervision for up to two years for inmates who were released and who are at a higher risk of re-offending, or who are in need of more reintegration and support.

sections.label: Reviews for incarcerated sexual offenders
sections.summary: The passage asks about reviews for incarcerated serious sexual offenders and how many would come under the regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For current offenders who are incarcerated – because they have committed serious sexual crimes, in the course of their custodial sentence – are there constant reviews done as to their re-integration later into the public after they have served their sentences?

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And in terms of the numbers of individuals that we are looking at who are currently serving sentences, how many people would the Minister estimate to come under the regime, based on whatever existing data the Government has?

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: As I have said many times in this House and outside, this is a matter of a very serious focus for the Home Team and the Singapore Prison Service, in that we focus a lot on rehabilitation.

sections.label: Yellow Ribbon Singapore job placement
sections.summary: YRSG takes a detailed approach to get and place released offenders in jobs and continues assisting them.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Yellow Ribbon Singapore (YRSG) takes a very detailed approach to try and get them jobs and place them on jobs when they leave and continues with other agencies to try and handhold and assist them thereafter.

sections.label: Risk of re-offending assessment
sections.summary: The Minister says assessing future risk of re-offending is part of the assessment but cannot give numbers.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: If the Leader of Opposition's question is do we assess the risk of re-offending in the way that I have described, for the future, that is part of the assessment, but I am unable to give the numbers.
